title: Stochastic Liouville-transport theory of light-atom interaction noise in thermal atomic vapors
authors: Shaoxin Yuan, Bin Wu, Mingyong Jing, Chaoyang Hu, Yan Peng, Tingting Li, Xingya Li, Wenguang Yang, Junyao Xie, Zongkai Liu, Hao Zhang, Linjie Zhang, Liantuan Xiao, Suotang Jia
abstract: Atom-light interaction noise can limit thermal-vapor sensing. Existing theories often treat internal-state dynamics, finite-mode atomic motion, and stochastic renewal separately, obscuring their coupled contributions to measured noise. We develop a general stochastic Liouville-transport theory, tested against polarization-resolved resonant Cs D$_2$ spectra. Joint experiment-theory analysis identifies atom-light noise below approximately 100 kHz as transit-dominated. Ballistic motion through the finite Gaussian mode modulates both the coupling-weighted effective atom number and trajectory-dependent Rabi coupling, producing predominantly common-mode noise. Boundary renewal introduces atoms with independently sampled ground-state sublevels, generating differential population fluctuations with opposite effects on the circular channels. Under an applied longitudinal magnetic field, experiment and theory show the same qualitative nonmonotonic change in common-mode suppression, supporting Zeeman redistribution of the channel responses. The framework can analyze noise in other thermal-atom sensors, including Rydberg-atom electric-field measurements.
summary: The authors develop a stochastic Liouville-transport theory to accurately model light-atom interaction noise in thermal atomic vapors. By jointly treating internal state evolution, finite-mode motion, and boundary renewal, the theory explains observed spectral features in Cs D2 spectra. This framework is crucial for advancing quantum sensing by providing a comprehensive understanding of noise sources beyond simple approximations.
main_problem: Atom-light interaction noise limits quantum sensing in thermal atomic vapors, and existing theories fail to account for the coupled effects of internal dynamics, motion, and renewal.
main_result: The theory successfully models how ballistic motion causes common-mode noise, while boundary renewal introduces differential fluctuations; it also reproduces field-dependent spectral changes observed in Cs D2 spectra.
method: A general stochastic Liouville-transport theory is developed to model the open quantum dynamics of atoms moving through a sensing region.
model_or_system: The system uses thermal atomic vapors (Cs D2) and models the evolution using an operator-valued phase-space density governed by a master equation incorporating Hamiltonian terms for hyperfine-Zeeman structure, detuning, and coupling, alongside transport and renewal terms.
key_observables: Polarization-resolved Power Spectral Densities (PSDs), specifically $S_+$, $S_-$, and the balanced difference $S_3(f)$, and the common-mode suppression factor $\Delta S$.
important_parameters: Noise frequency regime ($\approx 100$ kHz threshold), longitudinal magnetic field strength ($B_0$), and atomic constants related to hyperfine structure.
main_assumptions: The theory adopts a collisionless, recoil-free ballistic limit for transport and utilizes the Rotating-Wave Approximation (RWA) for Hamiltonian evaluation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optical setup for $\sigma^+$ and $\sigma^-$ detection, the hyperfine manifolds retained in the model, and plots showing the measured one-sided PSDs ($S_+$, $S_-$, $S_3$) across different magnetic fields.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the coupled stochastic Liouville theory, details the Hamiltonian and master equation governing dynamics (including transport/renewal), presents analysis of key observables like PSDs, and validates the model by reproducing experimental measurements for Cs D2 spectra under varying magnetic fields.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, unified theoretical framework for noise characterization in quantum sensors operating in realistic thermal environments, explicitly coupling spatial dynamics (transport) with internal quantum coherence (Liouville evolution).
